jobs.title: Senior Director, Product - Threat Intelligence & Detections
jobs.description:
At Arctic Wolf, you won’t just watch the cybersecurity industry evolve – you'll help lead the change. Our global Pack is made up of people who thrive on solving hard problems, moving fast, and building technology that protects organizations around the world. We’re proud to be recognized by Forbes, CNBC, Fortune, CRN, Gartner Peer Insights and IDC MarketScape – but what matters most is the work behind it: delivering real outcomes for customers through award winning innovation like our Aurora Platform.

If you’re looking for meaningful work, smart teammates and the chance to make a real impact in a high-growth company that’s redefining security operations, Arctic Wolf is the right place for you!

Our mission is simple: End Cyber Risk. We’re looking for Senior Director, Product - Threat Intelligence & Detection
to be part of making this happen.   

LOCATION
: This role is open to Remote-United States, Remote-Canada, Hybrid-Eden Prairie-MN-USA, Hybrid-Waterloo-ON-CAN.

This senior product management lead role for Arctic Wolf defines and evangelizes the commercial strategy and product roadmap for threat intelligence & threat hunting along with delivering on the platform strategy to drive detection efficacy and efficiency for the latest threats keeping our customers safe. You will collaborate with Architecture, Engineering, Security Research, and cross-functional teams to align product vision with company goals, guide strategic planning, and drive innovation and outcomes in threat intelligence, threat hunting and detection engineering. You will lead initiatives to map strategy to execution, commission research, define OKRs, and maintain alignment across product lines and stakeholders. As a respected leader in the cybersecurity space, you will influence organizational structure, drive cross-team buy-in, mentor others, and represent your group with transparency and integrity.

Role Scope

Presents at stakeholder meetings to communicate the vision and alignment with corporate strategy
Works with product principals and engineering leaders to communicate strategy and high-level roadmap for threat intelligence, detections, and AI related initiatives to Leadership, PM and Engineering teams
Participates in cross-functional efforts and co-design to ensure product initiatives leverage existing security research capabilities and avoid redundant development
Decides (with Architecture and Security Research leadership) when new threat detection or intelligence capabilities are sufficiently differentiated to create new products or platforms and deliver highest value in efficacy and efficiency
Creates vision and strategy presentations and documents that address high-level cybersecurity problems, emerging threat landscapes, and AI-driven solutions
Defines and drives the strategic vision for threat intelligence and threat hunting while overseeing the incubation of breakthrough threat detection capabilities that improve effectiveness of our products (MDR, EDR) and the SOC
Leads cross-functional teams through product development, fostering a culture of experimentation, rapid iteration, threat validation, and customer-centric innovation in security
Partners with executive leadership to align threat intelligence and AI initiatives with long-term business goals, ensuring resource allocation and portfolio management driving high-impact security outcomes

Knowledge & Experience

Deep expertise in threat intelligence, threat hunting, detection engineering, and security research practices and their application to product development
Demonstrated understanding of conversational AI, large language models (LLMs), and machine learning applications in cybersecurity and threat intelligence and or detections is a plus
Collaborate and run cross-functional backlog reviews for threat intelligence and detections; participate in other product line reviews to contribute to overall organizational prioritization
Commission research into possible strategies to address customer security problems and evolving threat landscapes
Identify OKRs for threat intelligence, threat hunting and detections in support of wider corporate goals
Identify follow-up analysis and insights into emerging threat patterns and their implications for product strategy

Complexity and Problem Solving

Communicates to teams about process changes and the value these bring—provides clarity and answers questions about threat detection innovation priorities
Works with Engineering and Labs leadership to align threat intelligence, detection, and AI strategies with company direction, then breaks out specific initiatives to implement and support the strategy
Propagates priorities and "big rocks" to product principals and technical leaders to create an overall threat intelligence and detection product roadmap
Helps other product teams understand how threat intelligence, detections, and AI capabilities enable faster, more effective threat response in their solutions
Identifies projects that shift priorities and communicates with stakeholders across threat intelligence, security operations, and engineering teams

Collaboration & Interaction

Aligns cross-functional teams (Security Research, Engineering, Sales, Go-to-Market) on threat intelligence product strategies & roadmap to successfully meet the business needs
Drives buy-in and support from the SOC, security research, engineering, sales, and broader organization improving our threat intel and detection efficacy and efficiency
Creates documentation required for calibration efforts and prepares for reviews with evidence of achievements to represent the threat intelligence and detection portfolio

Required Qualifications

7+ years of progressive experience in cybersecurity, with deep expertise in threat intelligence, threat hunting, detection engineering, incident response, or security research—this is non-negotiable
10+ years of product management experience, including 3+ years at a director level or equivalent managing complex, cross-functional teams delivering enterprise security products at scale
Proven track record of taking products from strategy through successful market launch, with quantifiable results in revenue growth, customer adoption, or competitive market share expansion
Executive presence with ability to speak credibly to technical and non-technical audiences about cybersecurity strategy, emerging threats, and security innovation

Preferred Qualifications

Background in Threat Intelligence, managed security services (MSS), managed detection and response (MDR), or security operations centers (SOCs)
Experience within a fast-growth cybersecurity company or within a security labs/innovation division focused on emerging threats or technologies
Active presence and network within the cybersecurity community, threat intelligence organizations, security research ecosystem, or industry consortiums is a plus

What We're Looking For

A seasoned cybersecurity leader and product strategist who brings deep technical credibility and hands-on threat intelligence experience combined with strong executive product management acumen. You understand evolving threat landscapes and advanced adversary tactics, have direct experience with threat intelligence analysis and threat hunting, and are passionate about applying emerging AI technologies to revolutionize how organizations detect and respond to threats. You can operate effectively at the executive level, balance strategic vision with execution discipline, and drive organizational alignment on complex, multi-year threat defense initiatives. You thrive in a fast-paced, innovation-focused environment and have the credibility to influence executive decision-making on security investments.

About Arctic Wolf

At Arctic Wolf, we foster a collaborative and inclusive work environment that thrives on diversity of thought, background, and culture. This is reflected in our multiple awards, including Top Workplace USA (2021-2025), Best Places to Work – USA (2021-2025), Great Place to Work – Canada (2021-2024), Great Place to Work – UK (2024-2026), and Kununu Top Company – Germany (2024-2026). Our commitment to bold growth and shaping the future of security operations is matched by our dedication to customer satisfaction, with over 10,000 customers worldwide and more than 2,000 channel partners globally. As we continue to expand globally and enhance our technology, Arctic Wolf remains the most trusted name in the industry.

Our Values

Arctic Wolf recognizes that success comes from delighting our customers, so we work together to ensure that happens every day. We believe in diversity and inclusion, and truly value the unique qualities and unique perspectives all employees bring to the organization. And we appreciate that—by protecting people’s and organizations’ sensitive data and seeking to end cyber risk— we get to work in an industry that is fundamental to the greater good.  

We celebrate unique perspectives by creating a platform for all voices to be heard through our Pack Unity program. We encourage all employees to join or create a new alliance. See more about our Pack Unity here.   

We also believe and practice corporate responsibility, and have recently joined the Pledge 1% Movement, ensuring that we continue to give back to our community. We know that through our mission to End Cyber Risk we will continue to engage and give back to our communities.  

All wolves receive compelling compensation and benefits packages, including:  

Equity for all employees 
Flexible time off and paid volunteer days 
RRSP contribution and matching
Training and career development programs 
Comprehensive private benefits plan including medical, mental health, dental, disability, life and AD&D, and value-added services 
Robust Employee Assistance Program (EAP) with mental health services 
Family-forming benefits, enhanced maternity benefits, and paid parental leave

Arctic Wolf is an Equal Opportunity Employer and considers applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, orientation, national origin, age, disability, genetics, or any other basis forbidden under federal, provincial, or local law. Arctic Wolf is committed to fostering a welcoming, accessible, respectful, and inclusive environment ensuring equal access and participation for people with disabilities. As such, we strive to make our entire experience as accessible as possible and provide accommodations as required for candidates and employees with disabilities and/or other specific needs where possible. Please let us know if you require any accommodation by emailing recruiting@arcticwolf.com.   View our Hiring Page to learn more about our application process.

Security Requirements

Conducts duties and responsibilities in accordance with AWN’s Information Security policies, standards, processes, and controls to protect the confidentiality, integrity and availability of AWN business information (in accordance with our employee handbook and corporate policies). 
Background checks are required for this position.  
This position may require access to information protected under U.S. export control laws and regulations, including the Export Administration Regulations (“EAR”).  Please note that, if applicable, an offer for employment will be conditioned on authorization to receive software or technology controlled under these U.S. export control laws and regulations. 

The base salary range for this job family is 164,000 to 287,000 CAD annually. This range reflects the base pay the company reasonably expects to offer for this position, aligned to the broader job family base pay structure. Actual base pay may vary based on skills, experience, and location, including job family level. In addition to base pay, Arctic Wolf offers variable incentive compensation, new hire equity grants, and a comprehensive benefits package.

jobs.title: Consulting Director, Financial Reporting (Workiva)
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Clearsulting is a global consulting company with the motivation to deliver positive change through digital finance. Our team consists of finance specialists that bring experience and technical capabilities across the spectrum of finance, including financial close, digital reporting, risk advisory, treasury and more.

Clearsulting stands by its culture, shaped by our five Core Values: GRIT, Growth Mindset, Joy, Accountability, and Teamwork. Our unwavering dedication to these principles has garnered national recognition for our strong leadership, innovative approach, and outstanding workplace environment. Below are some of the awards and accolades that honor our commitment to excellence:

Sunday Times Best Places to Work Award (2025-2026)
‘Great Place to Work’ Certified (2022-2026)
Fortune’s Best Workplaces in Consulting (2022-2024)
Inc. 5000 Fastest-Growing Private Companies in America (2020-2026)

Role

Consulting Director, Financial Reporting (Workiva)

Location:

Office Options: Hybrid or Remote. Team members residing within a 45 minute commuting radius of a Clearsulting office, we expect 4 days of in-person work per month, allowing flexibility choosing these days to accommodate client meetings, team syncs and individual schedules.
Travel Expectations: 20-40%

What You'll Do

Lead end-to-end Workiva implementation engagements for large, complex organizations, partnering with finance, accounting, and reporting stakeholders to design, implement, and deploy solutions that improve financial reporting and disclosure management.
Provide delivery leadership across Workiva implementation engagements, ensuring high-quality execution, adherence to leading practices, and successful client outcomes.
Build trusted relationships with client executives and project sponsors, proactively managing expectations, risks, scope, and overall engagement health.
Serve as a subject matter expert on Workiva capabilities and leading practices for financial reporting and disclosure management.
Mentor, coach, and develop consultants by providing technical guidance, reviewing work products, and supporting career development.
Collaborate with firm leadership to support business development activities, including proposal development, solution design, client presentations, and scoping of new opportunities.
Contribute to the development of implementation methodologies, reusable assets, accelerators, and internal best practices.
Effectively manage multiple client engagements while balancing quality, timelines, budgets, and stakeholder communications.
Consistently follow firm methodologies, quality standards, and delivery practices.

What You'll Bring

8+ years of experience leading Workiva implementations with responsibility for solution delivery, client engagement, and project leadership.
Deep expertise with the Workiva platform, including financial reporting, disclosure management, document collaboration, and related capabilities.
CPA required or preferred, or equivalent experience in financial reporting, SEC/SEDAR reporting, external reporting, technical accounting, or corporate accounting.
Strong understanding of financial statement preparation, reporting processes, disclosure management, and reporting controls.
Proven experience leading cross-functional project teams and managing client relationships with executive and senior finance stakeholders.
Demonstrated ability to deliver high-quality client solutions while managing project scope, risks, budgets, and timelines.
Experience facilitating executive workshops, gathering business requirements, and translating business needs into scalable Workiva solutions.
Exceptional consulting, communication, and presentation skills with the ability to influence executive audiences.
Experience supporting business development efforts, including proposals, solution demonstrations, estimating, and client pursuits.
Exceptional project management skills with experience managing multiple concurrent engagements.
Experience mentoring consultants and developing high-performing delivery teams.
Proficiency with Excel and financial data analysis

Nice-to-Haves

Experience in external reporting or controllership functions within a public company.
Experience with Workiva Wdata, Chains, SQL, and platform integrations.
Experience integrating Workiva with ERP systems such as SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics, or Workday.
Prior experience in management consulting or professional services.

Benefits That Benefit You

We want to cultivate a thriving culture and company—and we know that your health and well-being matter. We offer a benefits package and perks for our team members that include:

Medical, dental, and vision coverage
Unlimited PTO
Paid parental leave
Retirement plans
Flexible work environment
Cell phone reimbursement
Access to mental health apps
Life insurance and disability coverage
Opportunities for ad hoc bonuses

Excited about what we're doing but don't fit every requirement? No problem! At Clearsulting, we're forward-thinkers on a mission to redefine consulting excellence. We're all about diversity and inclusion, committed to assembling teams that mirror the world around us. So, if you're passionate about our mission, you could be the perfect fit for this role or another within our dynamic team. Don't hesitate to apply!

Learn more about Clearsulting by visiting https://www.clearsulting.com/careers/culture/

The compensation range for this position is $185,000-$246,000 CAD. We are committed to ensuring our offers reflect the value each candidate brings to the role. Final salary placement will be based on upon several factors, including, level of expertise, relevant work experience, technology certifications, educational background, geography and alignment with industry standards. This role is eligible for our bonus program.

Equal Opportunity Statement

Clearsulting is committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone has an equal opportunity to succeed. We make employment decisions based on qualifications, merit, and business needs, without discrimination on any basis protected by applicable local and statutory law.

jobs.title: Director, Control Brand Transformation
jobs.description:
Come make your difference in communities across Canada, where authenticity, trust and making connections is valued – as we shape the future of Canadian retail, together. Our unique position as one of the country's largest employers, coupled with our commitment to positively impact the lives of all Canadians, provides our colleagues a range of opportunities and experiences to help Canadians Live Life Well®.

At Loblaw Companies Limited, we succeed through collaboration and commitment and set a high bar for ourselves and those around us. Whether you are just starting your career, re-entering the workforce, or looking for a new job, this is where you belong.

The Impact You'll Make

As Director, Control Brand Transformation
, you will act as the SVP’s operating partner and central coordination point across the Control Brand transformation agenda. This is a newly created role accountable for helping the SVP translate strategic priorities into a clear operating rhythm, integrated workplans, executive-ready materials, decision forums, follow-ups, and cross-functional accountability. You will work directly with the SVP on priority workstreams including brand transformations, Board and executive materials, annual planning, governance, and critical cross-functional initiatives. This is a senior transformation orchestration role, coordinating across senior leaders and teams to ensure transformation workstreams move with pace, discipline, and clarity.

What You'll Do

Establish and manage the operating rhythm for the Control Brand transformation, including leadership meetings, workstream reviews, decision forums, executive updates, and follow-up mechanisms.
Ensure the SVP has clear visibility to priorities, risks, decisions required, stakeholder issues, and upcoming enterprise commitments.
Create the structure that enables the leadership team to operate with pace, alignment, and accountability.
Lead coordination across priority transformation workstreams, including brand transformation, annual planning, Board materials, executive reviews, and other SVP-led strategic initiatives.
Manage integrated timelines, milestones, deliverables, owners, and dependencies across workstreams.
Ensure workstreams are connected, sequenced, and not duplicative.
Work closely with the SVP to capture priorities, decisions, expectations, and actions from meetings and convert them into clear execution plans.
Ensure decisions are documented, owners are assigned, timelines are clear, and follow-through is actively managed.
Identify where issues require SVP intervention and where they can be resolved at the team level.
Establish clear governance for cross-functional workstreams, including agendas, pre-reads, decision logs, action trackers, escalation paths, and status reporting.
Proactively identify risks, gaps, misalignment, unresolved decisions, and resource constraints.
Drive resolution quickly by engaging the right stakeholders and escalating with clear options where needed.
Support the SVP in preparing high-quality materials for senior executive meetings, Board discussions, annual planning, transformation updates, and key decision forums.
Synthesize complex inputs into clear, concise narratives that are appropriate for executive audiences.
Ensure materials reflect strategic clarity, commercial logic, enterprise impact, and credible execution plans.
Act as the single point of coordination across teams and stakeholders for SVP-led transformation priorities.
Ensure seamless information flow between the SVP, direct reports, cross-functional partners, and enterprise stakeholders.
Travel with the SVP to key meetings where required, ensuring context, decisions, actions, and follow-ups are captured and advanced.

What You’ll Bring

8+ years of experience in strategy, transformation, program leadership, business operations, consulting, retail, CPG, or complex matrixed environments.
Proven experience leading multiple complex workstreams simultaneously.
Strong understanding of Loblaw or a similarly complex enterprise environment; prior LCL experience strongly preferred.
Strong ability to synthesize complex information into clear plans, narratives, and executive-ready materials.
Highly proactive, organized, action-oriented, and comfortable driving accountability across senior stakeholders.
Strong leadership presence with the ability to influence without formal authority.
Comfortable operating at both strategic and detailed levels.
Advanced communication, facilitation, and stakeholder management skills.

Our commitment to Sustainability and Social Impact is an essential part of the way we do business, and we focus our attention on areas where we can have the greatest impact. Our approach to sustainability and social impact is based on three pillars – Environment, Sourcing and Community – and we are constantly looking for ways to demonstrate leadership in these important areas. Our CORE Values – Care, Ownership, Respect and Excellence – guide all our decision-making and come to life through our Blue Culture. We offer our colleagues progressive careers, comprehensive training, flexibility, and other competitive benefits – these are some of the many reasons why we are one of Canada’s Top Employers, Canada’s Best Diversity Employers, Canada’s Greenest Employers & Canada’s Top Employers for Young People.

jobs.title: Director of Finance And Operations
jobs.description:
Director of Finance & Operations

Rubin & Co. LLP
(the firm) is seeking a highly organized, analytical, and collaborative Director of Finance & Operations
to join our growing team. This is a hands-on role, responsible for overseeing the firm’s financial operations, business processes, marketing initiatives, and special projects. Reporting to the Managing Director, the Director of Finance & Operations will work closely with firm leadership to ensure the effective management of the firm’s financial and operational functions, while supporting strategic initiatives and opportunities to improve efficiency, reporting, and business performance.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Management & Administration

Oversee the firm’s day-to-day financial operations, including accounts receivable, accounts payable, payroll, and cash management.
Manage the client accounting and billing functions, including client intake, time and billing systems, invoice preparation, billing adjustments and reconciliation, payment tracking, and collections.
Oversee the processing of vendor invoices and cheque requests, including authorizations, general ledger and tax coding, and compliance with firm policies and applicable Law Society of Ontario requirements.
Perform and oversee bank, trust, vendor, and general ledger reconciliations and ensure discrepancies are identified and resolved promptly.
Support monthly, quarterly, and year-end financial processes, including preparation of accurate financial reports and information for leadership and external advisors.
Prepare, monitor, and report on lawyer productivity, billing, and other key financial and operational metrics.
Review and process employee expense reports in accordance with firm policies.
Oversee office-related expenses and ensure appropriate general ledger categorization and financial organization.
Respond to accounting and financial inquiries in a timely, professional, and solutions-oriented manner.
Identify opportunities to improve financial processes, controls, systems, and procedures to increase efficiency and accuracy.

Business Operations & Special Projects

Work closely with the Managing Director and firm leadership on business planning, operational priorities, and strategic initiatives.
Develop, maintain, and report on key financial and operational performance metrics, including reviewing and improving operational processes, systems, and workflows firm-wide.
Prepare financial and operational information and analyses to support leadership decision-making.
Support the implementation and optimization of technology, systems, and business processes.
Coordinate and manage special projects and strategic initiatives as required.
Assist with vendor management, contracts, office administration, and other business operations.
Identify opportunities to improve the firm’s overall efficiency, client experience, and internal processes.
Take ownership of projects from planning through execution, ensuring deadlines and deliverables are met.

Marketing & Communications

Support and oversee the execution of the firm’s marketing and communications strategy in collaboration with the Managing Director and external marketing resources.
Manage and coordinate the firm’s marketing initiatives, from development through to distribution, via LinkedIn, email communications, newsletters, website content, and other digital communications.
Manage firm webinars and events, including registration, promotional materials, communications, logistics, and post-event follow-up.
Maintain and coordinate updates to the firm’s website, ensuring content is current, accurate, and aligned with the firm’s brand.
Manage and maintain the firm’s mailing lists and subscription databases, including ongoing compliance with applicable CASL requirements.
Monitor and report on marketing and communications analytics, including email, website, social media, and webinar performance.
Work with internal and external stakeholders to develop and implement marketing projects and initiatives.
Identify opportunities to improve the firm’s visibility, communications, and engagement with clients and professional audiences.

Knowledge, Skills, & Experience

5 years of progressive experience in finance, accounting, operations, business administration, or a related role; experience working in a law firm or other professional services environment is required.
Experience managing financial operations, including billing, accounts payable/receivable, reconciliations, cash management, and financial reporting.
Accounting, finance, or business education or designation (CPA, CMA, CGA, accounting/finance diploma or degree) is an asset.
Experience with QuickBooks Online and Clio or similar accounting and practice management systems is an asset.
Experience in marketing, communications, project management, or business development is required.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret financial and operational information and identify trends and opportunities.
Highly organized and detail-oriented, with excellent time management and the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
Strong written and verbal communication skills and a professional, client service-oriented approach.
Ability to work independently, take initiative, and exercise sound judgment.
Comfortable working in a fast-paced, collaborative environment with a high degree of accountability.
Strong proficiency with Microsoft Office, particularly Excel.
Positive, solutions-oriented attitude and demonstrated ability to work effectively as part of a team.

Why Join Rubin & Co. LLP?

Rubin & Co. LLP is a growing workplace investigations and consulting firm committed to providing thoughtful, high-quality services to organizations navigating complex workplace matters. We offer an opportunity to work closely with firm leadership and play a meaningful role in the continued growth and development of the business. If this position and our firm are of interest to you, please send your resume in confidence to careers@rubinandco.ca.

We thank all applicants for their interest in joining our team. However, only those selected for an interview will be contacted. **No agencies please.**
To learn more about Rubin & Co. LLP, visit www.rubinandco.ca.

jobs.title: Executive Director - Technology Risk Services - IT Audit
jobs.description:
Overview

At KPMG in Canada, our people bring their unique perspectives to Canada’s most important challenges. Here, you can build momentum that reaches beyond our business, develop skills for the future, and take ownership of your career with support at every stage. Join a firm where your career can make a difference.

Our Technology Risk Services team is growing. We are looking for an executive director
to join our dynamic team in Montreal.

Our IT audit service lines include

Assisting KPMG Audit teams in both audit of technology and in leveraging technology in financial statement audits and integrated audits of financial statements and internal controls. Audit technology-related risks and controls and assist our Audit teams in addressing complex technology topics, including impacts of client artificial intelligence (AI) usage on the audits. Also, perform system implementation assessments in support of external audits at our clients.
Formal assurance on systems, processes, and controls, including Audits of Service Organization Controls (i.e., SOC 1 engagements under CSAE 3416, SSAE 18, and/or ISAE 3402), SOC 2 and SOC 3 engagements (systems security & reliability assurance), and other standards.

What You Will Do

Working closely with our Audit teams as the IT executive in charge for some client where permissible to scope processes, conducting assessments of IT risks and controls, including general IT controls and automated controls embedded within information systems in support of our external audit engagements.
Overseeing, conducting IT audit procedures (e.g., IT risk assessments, General IT Controls, IT Application Controls, large System Implementations and Data Conversions) in support of financial statement audits and internal controls over financial reporting.
Overseeing, conducting IT internal audit and third-party attestation engagements such as CSAE 3416 / SSAE 18 / SOC 1 and SOC 2 reports.
Overseeing the planning, managing, and completing IT Audit project tasks including liaising with client and KPMG teams; collecting, testing, and exploring information; documenting and evaluating IT processes, controls, policies, strategies; and performing detailed quality assurance review and feedback on the work of others.
Communicating (written and verbal) findings and recommendations to the client including technical and business communication to management through the preparation of reports and analyses; preparation of advisory and assurance reports and related deliverables.
Guiding field engagement teams as well as coaching junior staff members.
Influencing and contributing to other practice initiatives, including but not limited to knowledge sharing, training, HR initiatives, and practice management activities.
Supporting regulators file inspections process.
Supporting go-to-market initiatives for business development.

What You Bring To The Role

Bachelor’s degree (or higher) in Business or Computer Science degree required, ideally with a major in accounting.
Completion of one or a combination of the following designations CA, CISA, CISSP.
Minimum of 10 years of combined relevant experience in IT Audit (internal and/or external audit) within a large consulting practice.
Strong understanding and experience with IT Integrated Audits and controls-based audits
Strong understanding and experience with third-party assurance reports (e.g., CSAE 3416, SSAE 18, SOC 2) is required.
Experience with the identification and or evaluation of process level controls in large system transformation projects involving SAP and or Oracle.
Experience in the testing of controls in different IT environments, like SAP, Oracle, Unix, Linux, AS400, Mainframe, etc.
Experience within an external audit practice auditing client in the Financial Services, Technology and Telecom, and Mining industry.
Ability to work both, with little supervision and within a team environment.
Excellent communication skills being able to express insights, both written and orally.
Demonstrated ability to learn and succeed in a fast-paced environment.
Attention to detail and strong organization and investigative skills.
Strong understanding of business risks and audit risks.
Have a high degree of personal confidence, enthusiasm, and drive.

new_jobs.title: Senior Director, Product - Threat Intelligence & Detections
new_jobs.description:
At Arctic Wolf, you won’t just watch the cybersecurity industry evolve – you'll help lead the change. Our global Pack is made up of people who thrive on solving hard problems, moving fast, and building technology that protects organizations around the world. We’re proud to be recognized by Forbes, CNBC, Fortune, CRN, Gartner Peer Insights and IDC MarketScape – but what matters most is the work behind it: delivering real outcomes for customers through award winning innovation like our Aurora Platform.

If you’re looking for meaningful work, smart teammates and the chance to make a real impact in a high-growth company that’s redefining security operations, Arctic Wolf is the right place for you!

Our mission is simple: End Cyber Risk. We’re looking for Senior Director, Product - Threat Intelligence & Detection
to be part of making this happen.   

LOCATION
: This role is open to Remote-United States, Remote-Canada, Hybrid-Eden Prairie-MN-USA, Hybrid-Waterloo-ON-CAN.

This senior product management lead role for Arctic Wolf defines and evangelizes the commercial strategy and product roadmap for threat intelligence & threat hunting along with delivering on the platform strategy to drive detection efficacy and efficiency for the latest threats keeping our customers safe. You will collaborate with Architecture, Engineering, Security Research, and cross-functional teams to align product vision with company goals, guide strategic planning, and drive innovation and outcomes in threat intelligence, threat hunting and detection engineering. You will lead initiatives to map strategy to execution, commission research, define OKRs, and maintain alignment across product lines and stakeholders. As a respected leader in the cybersecurity space, you will influence organizational structure, drive cross-team buy-in, mentor others, and represent your group with transparency and integrity.

Role Scope

Presents at stakeholder meetings to communicate the vision and alignment with corporate strategy
Works with product principals and engineering leaders to communicate strategy and high-level roadmap for threat intelligence, detections, and AI related initiatives to Leadership, PM and Engineering teams
Participates in cross-functional efforts and co-design to ensure product initiatives leverage existing security research capabilities and avoid redundant development
Decides (with Architecture and Security Research leadership) when new threat detection or intelligence capabilities are sufficiently differentiated to create new products or platforms and deliver highest value in efficacy and efficiency
Creates vision and strategy presentations and documents that address high-level cybersecurity problems, emerging threat landscapes, and AI-driven solutions
Defines and drives the strategic vision for threat intelligence and threat hunting while overseeing the incubation of breakthrough threat detection capabilities that improve effectiveness of our products (MDR, EDR) and the SOC
Leads cross-functional teams through product development, fostering a culture of experimentation, rapid iteration, threat validation, and customer-centric innovation in security
Partners with executive leadership to align threat intelligence and AI initiatives with long-term business goals, ensuring resource allocation and portfolio management driving high-impact security outcomes

Knowledge & Experience

Deep expertise in threat intelligence, threat hunting, detection engineering, and security research practices and their application to product development
Demonstrated understanding of conversational AI, large language models (LLMs), and machine learning applications in cybersecurity and threat intelligence and or detections is a plus
Collaborate and run cross-functional backlog reviews for threat intelligence and detections; participate in other product line reviews to contribute to overall organizational prioritization
Commission research into possible strategies to address customer security problems and evolving threat landscapes
Identify OKRs for threat intelligence, threat hunting and detections in support of wider corporate goals
Identify follow-up analysis and insights into emerging threat patterns and their implications for product strategy

Complexity and Problem Solving

Communicates to teams about process changes and the value these bring—provides clarity and answers questions about threat detection innovation priorities
Works with Engineering and Labs leadership to align threat intelligence, detection, and AI strategies with company direction, then breaks out specific initiatives to implement and support the strategy
Propagates priorities and "big rocks" to product principals and technical leaders to create an overall threat intelligence and detection product roadmap
Helps other product teams understand how threat intelligence, detections, and AI capabilities enable faster, more effective threat response in their solutions
Identifies projects that shift priorities and communicates with stakeholders across threat intelligence, security operations, and engineering teams

Collaboration & Interaction

Aligns cross-functional teams (Security Research, Engineering, Sales, Go-to-Market) on threat intelligence product strategies & roadmap to successfully meet the business needs
Drives buy-in and support from the SOC, security research, engineering, sales, and broader organization improving our threat intel and detection efficacy and efficiency
Creates documentation required for calibration efforts and prepares for reviews with evidence of achievements to represent the threat intelligence and detection portfolio

Required Qualifications

7+ years of progressive experience in cybersecurity, with deep expertise in threat intelligence, threat hunting, detection engineering, incident response, or security research—this is non-negotiable
10+ years of product management experience, including 3+ years at a director level or equivalent managing complex, cross-functional teams delivering enterprise security products at scale
Proven track record of taking products from strategy through successful market launch, with quantifiable results in revenue growth, customer adoption, or competitive market share expansion
Executive presence with ability to speak credibly to technical and non-technical audiences about cybersecurity strategy, emerging threats, and security innovation

Preferred Qualifications

Background in Threat Intelligence, managed security services (MSS), managed detection and response (MDR), or security operations centers (SOCs)
Experience within a fast-growth cybersecurity company or within a security labs/innovation division focused on emerging threats or technologies
Active presence and network within the cybersecurity community, threat intelligence organizations, security research ecosystem, or industry consortiums is a plus

What We're Looking For

A seasoned cybersecurity leader and product strategist who brings deep technical credibility and hands-on threat intelligence experience combined with strong executive product management acumen. You understand evolving threat landscapes and advanced adversary tactics, have direct experience with threat intelligence analysis and threat hunting, and are passionate about applying emerging AI technologies to revolutionize how organizations detect and respond to threats. You can operate effectively at the executive level, balance strategic vision with execution discipline, and drive organizational alignment on complex, multi-year threat defense initiatives. You thrive in a fast-paced, innovation-focused environment and have the credibility to influence executive decision-making on security investments.

About Arctic Wolf

At Arctic Wolf, we foster a collaborative and inclusive work environment that thrives on diversity of thought, background, and culture. This is reflected in our multiple awards, including Top Workplace USA (2021-2025), Best Places to Work – USA (2021-2025), Great Place to Work – Canada (2021-2024), Great Place to Work – UK (2024-2026), and Kununu Top Company – Germany (2024-2026). Our commitment to bold growth and shaping the future of security operations is matched by our dedication to customer satisfaction, with over 10,000 customers worldwide and more than 2,000 channel partners globally. As we continue to expand globally and enhance our technology, Arctic Wolf remains the most trusted name in the industry.

Our Values

Arctic Wolf recognizes that success comes from delighting our customers, so we work together to ensure that happens every day. We believe in diversity and inclusion, and truly value the unique qualities and unique perspectives all employees bring to the organization. And we appreciate that—by protecting people’s and organizations’ sensitive data and seeking to end cyber risk— we get to work in an industry that is fundamental to the greater good.  

We celebrate unique perspectives by creating a platform for all voices to be heard through our Pack Unity program. We encourage all employees to join or create a new alliance. See more about our Pack Unity here.   

We also believe and practice corporate responsibility, and have recently joined the Pledge 1% Movement, ensuring that we continue to give back to our community. We know that through our mission to End Cyber Risk we will continue to engage and give back to our communities.  

All wolves receive compelling compensation and benefits packages, including:  

Equity for all employees 
Flexible time off and paid volunteer days 
RRSP contribution and matching
Training and career development programs 
Comprehensive private benefits plan including medical, mental health, dental, disability, life and AD&D, and value-added services 
Robust Employee Assistance Program (EAP) with mental health services 
Family-forming benefits, enhanced maternity benefits, and paid parental leave

Arctic Wolf is an Equal Opportunity Employer and considers applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, orientation, national origin, age, disability, genetics, or any other basis forbidden under federal, provincial, or local law. Arctic Wolf is committed to fostering a welcoming, accessible, respectful, and inclusive environment ensuring equal access and participation for people with disabilities. As such, we strive to make our entire experience as accessible as possible and provide accommodations as required for candidates and employees with disabilities and/or other specific needs where possible. Please let us know if you require any accommodation by emailing recruiting@arcticwolf.com.   View our Hiring Page to learn more about our application process.

Security Requirements

Conducts duties and responsibilities in accordance with AWN’s Information Security policies, standards, processes, and controls to protect the confidentiality, integrity and availability of AWN business information (in accordance with our employee handbook and corporate policies). 
Background checks are required for this position.  
This position may require access to information protected under U.S. export control laws and regulations, including the Export Administration Regulations (“EAR”).  Please note that, if applicable, an offer for employment will be conditioned on authorization to receive software or technology controlled under these U.S. export control laws and regulations. 

The base salary range for this job family is 164,000 to 287,000 CAD annually. This range reflects the base pay the company reasonably expects to offer for this position, aligned to the broader job family base pay structure. Actual base pay may vary based on skills, experience, and location, including job family level. In addition to base pay, Arctic Wolf offers variable incentive compensation, new hire equity grants, and a comprehensive benefits package.

Come make your difference in communities across Canada, where authenticity, trust and making connections is valued – as we shape the future of Canadian retail, together. At Loblaw Companies Limited, we succeed through collaboration and commitment and set a high bar for ourselves and those around us. Whether you are just starting your career, re-entering the workforce, or looking for a new job, this is where you belong.

The Impact You'll Make

As Director, Control Brand Transformation
, you will act as the SVP’s operating partner and central coordination point across the Control Brand transformation agenda. This is a newly created role accountable for helping the SVP translate strategic priorities into a clear operating rhythm, integrated workplans, executive-ready materials, decision forums, follow-ups, and cross-functional accountability. You will work directly with the SVP on priority workstreams including brand transformations, Board and executive materials, annual planning, governance, and critical cross-functional initiatives. This is a senior transformation orchestration role, coordinating across senior leaders and teams to ensure transformation workstreams move with pace, discipline, and clarity.

What You'll Do

Establish and manage the operating rhythm for the Control Brand transformation, including leadership meetings, workstream reviews, decision forums, executive updates, and follow-up mechanisms.
Ensure the SVP has clear visibility to priorities, risks, decisions required, stakeholder issues, and upcoming enterprise commitments.
Create the structure that enables the leadership team to operate with pace, alignment, and accountability.
Lead coordination across priority transformation workstreams, including brand transformation, annual planning, Board materials, executive reviews, and other SVP-led strategic initiatives.
Manage integrated timelines, milestones, deliverables, owners, and dependencies across workstreams.

Highly proactive, organized, action-oriented, and comfortable driving accountability across senior stakeholders.

new_jobs.title: Director of Finance And Operations
new_jobs.description:
Director of Finance & Operations

Rubin & Co. LLP
(the firm) is seeking a highly organized, analytical, and collaborative Director of Finance & Operations
to join our growing team. This is a hands-on role, responsible for overseeing the firm’s financial operations, business processes, marketing initiatives, and special projects. Reporting to the Managing Director, the Director of Finance & Operations will work closely with firm leadership to ensure the effective management of the firm’s financial and operational functions, while supporting strategic initiatives and opportunities to improve efficiency, reporting, and business performance.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Management & Administration

Oversee the firm’s day-to-day financial operations, including accounts receivable, accounts payable, payroll, and cash management.
Manage the client accounting and billing functions, including client intake, time and billing systems, invoice preparation, billing adjustments and reconciliation, payment tracking, and collections.
Oversee the processing of vendor invoices and cheque requests, including authorizations, general ledger and tax coding, and compliance with firm policies and applicable Law Society of Ontario requirements.
Perform and oversee bank, trust, vendor, and general ledger reconciliations and ensure discrepancies are identified and resolved promptly.
Support monthly, quarterly, and year-end financial processes, including preparation of accurate financial reports and information for leadership and external advisors.
Prepare, monitor, and report on lawyer productivity, billing, and other key financial and operational metrics.
Review and process employee expense reports in accordance with firm policies.
Oversee office-related expenses and ensure appropriate general ledger categorization and financial organization.
Respond to accounting and financial inquiries in a timely, professional, and solutions-oriented manner.
Identify opportunities to improve financial processes, controls, systems, and procedures to increase efficiency and accuracy.

Business Operations & Special Projects

Work closely with the Managing Director and firm leadership on business planning, operational priorities, and strategic initiatives.
Develop, maintain, and report on key financial and operational performance metrics, including reviewing and improving operational processes, systems, and workflows firm-wide.
Prepare financial and operational information and analyses to support leadership decision-making.
Support the implementation and optimization of technology, systems, and business processes.
Coordinate and manage special projects and strategic initiatives as required.
Assist with vendor management, contracts, office administration, and other business operations.
Identify opportunities to improve the firm’s overall efficiency, client experience, and internal processes.
Take ownership of projects from planning through execution, ensuring deadlines and deliverables are met.

Marketing & Communications

Support and oversee the execution of the firm’s marketing and communications strategy in collaboration with the Managing Director and external marketing resources.
Manage and coordinate the firm’s marketing initiatives, from development through to distribution, via LinkedIn, email communications, newsletters, website content, and other digital communications.
Manage firm webinars and events, including registration, promotional materials, communications, logistics, and post-event follow-up.
Maintain and coordinate updates to the firm’s website, ensuring content is current, accurate, and aligned with the firm’s brand.
Manage and maintain the firm’s mailing lists and subscription databases, including ongoing compliance with applicable CASL requirements.
Monitor and report on marketing and communications analytics, including email, website, social media, and webinar performance.
Work with internal and external stakeholders to develop and implement marketing projects and initiatives.
Identify opportunities to improve the firm’s visibility, communications, and engagement with clients and professional audiences.

Knowledge, Skills, & Experience

5 years of progressive experience in finance, accounting, operations, business administration, or a related role; experience working in a law firm or other professional services environment is required.
Experience managing financial operations, including billing, accounts payable/receivable, reconciliations, cash management, and financial reporting.
Accounting, finance, or business education or designation (CPA, CMA, CGA, accounting/finance diploma or degree) is an asset.
Experience with QuickBooks Online and Clio or similar accounting and practice management systems is an asset.
Experience in marketing, communications, project management, or business development is required.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret financial and operational information and identify trends and opportunities.
Highly organized and detail-oriented, with excellent time management and the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
Strong written and verbal communication skills and a professional, client service-oriented approach.
Ability to work independently, take initiative, and exercise sound judgment.
Comfortable working in a fast-paced, collaborative environment with a high degree of accountability.
Strong proficiency with Microsoft Office, particularly Excel.
Positive, solutions-oriented attitude and demonstrated ability to work effectively as part of a team.

Why Join Rubin & Co. LLP?

Rubin & Co. LLP is a growing workplace investigations and consulting firm committed to providing thoughtful, high-quality services to organizations navigating complex workplace matters. We offer an opportunity to work closely with firm leadership and play a meaningful role in the continued growth and development of the business. If this position and our firm are of interest to you, please send your resume in confidence to careers@rubinandco.ca.

We thank all applicants for their interest in joining our team. However, only those selected for an interview will be contacted. **No agencies please.**
To learn more about Rubin & Co. LLP, visit www.rubinandco.ca.
